summary: Independent HG-BACKFILL-FIDELITY audit on PR #274 exact head 5251998df21e8f7f78cae5c046d346496cc65a28 finds one remaining source-only blocker: custom PolicyConfig can execute metatable-backed field access before validation. FidelityManager.new copies/dereferences sourceConfig before proving it plain/metatable-free, and exported evaluatePolicy validates config fields without a preceding plain-table fence. The separately owned test-adversary PR #325 / head 90f6a924106a23c9e1cecfd240560852e774198d isolates this exact no-execute contract; its canonical CI reaches Pure Luau tests and fails there as intended against current production. Audit verdict is REQUEST_CHANGES until primary consumes that proof and rejects non-plain PolicyConfig before first field access. Existing callback transactional/reentry/accounting closure is patch-locally sound and should be preserved.
evidence: PR #274 audit review 4904313618 records the exact-head REQUEST_CHANGES verdict.
src/shared/Physics/FidelityManager.luau@5251998: new(config) calls copyConfig(sourceConfig) before validateConfig; copyConfig directly reads config fields.
src/shared/Physics/FidelityManager.luau@5251998: evaluatePolicy resolves custom config then calls validateConfig, whose field reads/comparisons precede any type/metatable guard.

PR #325 / head 90f6a924106a23c9e1cecfd240560852e774198d adds constructor/pure-policy PolicyConfig no-execute regressions; CI run 31473342951 passes format/lint/Luau/static audits then fails at Pure Luau tests against current production as intended.
PR #274 exact-head canonical CI run 31471785808 passes, so the blocker is semantic/adversarial rather than toolchain breakage.
